# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

I can see the bomb clearly: the display reads 0, the light is yellow, and the large button is labeled “PUSH TO DEFUSE.” The three wires, from top to bottom, are red, blue, and green. I am telling the Blind this so they can match it against the manual and determine the safe action. The Mute’s Morse-like gesture message appears to begin “BLUE,” but the remainder is unclear, so I will not infer an action from it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Display 0. Light yellow. Large button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires top to bottom: red, blue, green.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires top to bottom red blue green. Your gesture message decoded clearly only as BLUE; the rest was unclear.")
wait()
```

The bomb is still unchanged. The Mute’s gesture code is Morse-like: the clear portion says “DO NOT PUSH.” The remaining groups appear intended to say “CUT BLUE,” though two letter groups do not match standard Morse exactly. Since the button is explicitly a push-to-defuse control but the Mute’s manual instruction warns against pushing, I will relay the probable instruction and the uncertainty. The blue wire is the second wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's Morse clearly says DO NOT PUSH. The remaining message appears intended as CUT BLUE, but two Morse groups are malformed. Blue is wire 2, between red and green.")
speak(to="mute", text="I decode your message as DO NOT PUSH, then probably CUT BLUE, but the Morse groups for U and L appear malformed. Please clarify.")
wait()
```

The bomb remains unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large “PUSH TO DEFUSE” button, and wires red, blue, green from top to bottom. I cannot reliably decode the Mute’s latest gesture stream; interpreting it as Morse produces nonsensical text, so I will not recommend cutting a wire or pressing the button. Blind should rely on the manual and request a clearer encoding from Mute.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red blue green top to bottom. I cannot reliably decode Mute's latest gesture stream; Morse interpretation is incoherent. Do not act on my wire or button guess.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your latest gesture message is not decoding coherently as Morse. Please repeat the manual instruction using clear Morse: thumbs-down dash, thumbs-up dot, OK between letters, stop-hand between words.")
wait()
```

The bomb is unchanged. The Mute has sent two gesture strings, but even the shorter one does not decode into a coherent Morse instruction under the previously established convention (thumbs-up dot, thumbs-down dash, OK between letters, stop-hand between words). I will not infer a wire or button action from corrupted text. I am relaying the uncertainty and asking the Blind to wait.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red blue green. Mute sent two Morse-like messages, but neither decodes coherently enough to authorize an action. Do not press or cut anything yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I still cannot decode the gesture strings reliably. Please resend only the final action, slowly, with OK between every letter and stop-hand between words, using thumbs-up dot and thumbs-down dash.")
wait()
```
